description: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of results across three difficulty levels – easy, medium, and hard – for a “Zero-Shot” experiment, likely representing the success rate of a model. The chart is composed of three distinct pie charts, one for each difficulty level. The “easy” chart contains three slices: a large teal slice labeled “N+K+” representing 55.4%, a smaller orange slice labeled “N–K+” representing 4.6%, and a larger gold slice labeled “N+K–” representing 38.3%. The “medium” chart also has three slices: a teal slice labeled “N+K+” representing 58.8%, an orange slice labeled “N–K+” representing 4.8%, and a gold slice labeled “N+K–” representing 35.4%. The “hard” chart contains four slices: a teal slice labeled “N+K+” representing 37.3%, an orange slice labeled “N–K+” representing 6.7%, a gold slice labeled “N+K–” representing 37.9%, and a red slice labeled “N+K–” representing 18.1%. Each chart includes percentage labels displayed inside the slices, and each chart also includes a legend identifying the labels and corresponding colors. The slices within each chart appear to be ordered from largest to smallest based on their visual proportion.
